The Command also arrested a 26-year-old woman, Saadiya Sahabi, who is the paternal aunt of the victim, in connection with the abduction.
The rescue was announced on Friday, November 13, 2026, in a statement by the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Yazid Abubakar, on behalf of the Commissioner of Police, Zamfara State Command.
According to the police, the case began on October 30, 2026, at about 11:30am when detectives attached to the State Intelligence Department (SID) received a formal complaint from one Abdulganiyu Sahabi, a resident of Kaura Namoda Local Government Area.
The complainant reported that his three-year-old daughter had been abducted by an unknown person on October 28, 2026.
He further disclosed that on October 29, 2026, he received a telephone call from a concealed number. The caller claimed to have his daughter in custody and demanded a ransom of Ten Million Naira (₦10,000,000) for her release.
Upon receipt of the report, the Commissioner of Police, Zamfara State Command, CP A.M. Bello,, immediately directed the State Intelligence Department to commence a thorough investigation and ensure the safe rescue of the abducted child.
Following days of sustained intelligence gathering, technical analysis and collaboration with strategic partners, operatives successfully traced and arrested the suspect on November 10, 2026, at Bela District, Bungudu Local Government Area of Zamfara State. The victim was also rescued safely. Is
Preliminary investigation identified the suspect as Saadiya Sahabi, aged 26, who is the younger sister of the victim’s father, sharing the same biological father but having different mothers.
During interrogation, the suspect allegedly confessed to her involvement in the crime.
The Command said investigation is ongoing to establish the full circumstances surrounding the incident and to identify and apprehend any other persons who may have participated in the crime.
The rescued child was taken for medical examination and, after necessary assessment, was formally reunited with her parents on *November 12, 2026.
The Commissioner of Police commended the operatives of the State Intelligence Department for their professionalism, dedication and effective application of intelligence-led policing, which culminated in the successful rescue of the child.
He reiterated the Command’s unwavering commitment to protecting lives and property, particularly vulnerable members of society, and ensuring that all persons found culpable of kidnapping and other criminal activities are brought to justice.
The Command urged members of the public to remain vigilant, strengthen cooperation with security agencies and promptly report suspicious movements or activities to the nearest police station.
